title: The point-contact transistor demonstrates solid-state amplification
significance: Bell Labs developed the point-contact transistor in 1947. Controlling electrical behavior in a semiconductor opened a route beyond vacuum tubes toward much smaller active circuits; modern AI hardware descends from that physical switching and amplification foundation.

title: Kilby demonstrates a working integrated circuit
significance: On September 12, 1958, Jack Kilby demonstrated a working circuit at Texas Instruments with circuit elements formed in a semiconductor piece. Integration began replacing the assembly of many separate components with fabrication of related functions together.

source.title: Texas Instruments: The origin of the integrated circuit

title: Noyce files a patent for planar semiconductor interconnection
significance: Robert Noyce filed the application underlying US2981877 on July 30, 1959. Metal connections over an insulating surface supplied a practical route to connecting multiple semiconductor elements, complementing the integrated-circuit concept with a manufacturable interconnection approach.

source.title: Robert Noyce: US2981877A, Semiconductor device-and-lead structure

title: Kahng files an insulated-gate field-effect device patent
significance: Dawon Kahng’s US3102230 application was filed on May 31, 1960. The insulated-gate field-effect approach made an electric field the control mechanism for a semiconductor channel, a foundation for the MOS devices that later dominated dense integrated logic. This is a patent-filing milestone, not a claim that the first working device appeared on that date.

source.title: Dawon Kahng: US3102230A, Electric field controlled semiconductor device

title: Wanlass files complementary field-effect circuitry
significance: Complementary n- and p-channel switching provided a path to low standby-power logic. The patent was filed in 1963 and granted in 1967.

title: Dennard’s DRAM cell patent is granted
significance: Robert Dennard’s field-effect memory patent, filed in 1967 after his 1966 work at IBM, was granted on June 4, 1968. A compact access device and charge-storage element established the basis for dense dynamic memory, with periodic restoration as part of normal operation.

source.title: Robert Dennard: US3387286A, Field-effect transistor memory

title: Intel introduces the 4004 microprocessor
significance: Intel introduced the 4004 in November 1971. Integrating a programmable CPU on a chip made it practical to reuse a hardware design for different instruction sequences, advancing the general-purpose control layer that still coordinates modern accelerator systems.

source.title: Intel: Announcing a New Era of Integrated Electronics

title: Fully integrated copper wiring demonstrated
significance: IBM reported integrated CMOS with multiple copper wiring levels, addressing interconnect resistance together with fabrication and reliability. This was a wiring breakthrough, not simply a smaller transistor.

source.title: Edelstein et al. — Full Copper Wiring, IEDM 1997

title: GeForce 256 integrates transform and lighting into a GPU
significance: NVIDIA’s GeForce 256 moved additional graphics geometry work into an integrated graphics processor. This product milestone helped establish the GPU as a powerful parallel processor; earlier graphics processors already existed, and the modern general-purpose compute model arrived through later architectural and software developments.

title: Distributed word representations in a neural language model
significance: Bengio and colleagues jointly learned word vectors and a sequence probability model, showing how shared continuous representations could generalize beyond previously observed word sequences.

source.title: Bengio et al. — A Neural Probabilistic Language Model

title: CUDA opens GPU execution to general computation
significance: NVIDIA introduced the CUDA architecture in 2006, allowing computational workloads to use GPU throughput without expressing the problem through graphics APIs. A programmable parallel hierarchy gave researchers a practical path from scientific and numerical code to large numbers of GPU execution units.

title: High-k and metal gates enter Intel’s 45 nm generation
significance: Hafnium-based dielectric and metal electrodes addressed leakage and gate-control limits of thinning silicon dioxide and polysilicon. The 45 nm name identifies the process generation.

source.title: Intel — High-k and Metal Gate Research

title: Pre-production NXE:3100 EUV system ships
significance: The pre-production system moved 13.5 nm lithography closer to manufacturing integration. It preceded later production platforms and should not be mistaken for immediate universal EUV adoption.

source.title: ASML — Making EUV: From Lab to Fab

title: Intel announces 3D Tri-Gate for the 22 nm generation
significance: Multisurface gate control moved a major production logic platform beyond planar transistor geometry. This is an Intel commercialization milestone, not the first invention of every FinFET concept.

title: TSMC CoWoS enters volume production
significance: TSMC dates CoWoS volume production to 2012. The packaging platform evolved to integrate multiple logic dies and high-bandwidth memory through dense local interconnect, making the package an important part of system architecture.

source.title: TSMC: CoWoS platform history and technology

title: Adam combines momentum with adaptive scaling
significance: Kingma and Ba released the Adam preprint in December 2014; its conference publication followed at ICLR 2015. The method maintains first and second gradient-moment estimates.

source.title: Kingma & Ba — Adam: A Method for Stochastic Optimization

title: Subword BPE enters neural translation
significance: Sennrich, Haddow, and Birch adapted byte-pair segmentation to represent rare words as subword sequences. The preprint appeared in 2015; the conference paper followed at ACL 2016.

source.title: Sennrich et al. — Neural Machine Translation of Rare Words with Subword Units

title: Pascal P100 combines HBM2 packaging with NVLink
significance: Announced on April 5, 2016, Tesla P100 brought HBM2 memory in a CoWoS package together with NVLink in NVIDIA’s Pascal accelerator platform. Faster local memory and GPU-to-GPU communication addressed data movement alongside arithmetic, anticipating the system bottlenecks of larger neural networks.

title: Layer normalization removes dependence on batch statistics
significance: Ba, Kiros, and Hinton proposed normalization within a training example, with the same normalization computation at training and inference. This became useful for sequence models with varying batch conditions.

title: Attention Is All You Need
significance: The Transformer demonstrated a sequence architecture organized around attention, enabling extensive parallel work during training.

title: Volta introduces NVIDIA Tensor Cores
significance: NVIDIA announced Volta and Tesla V100 on May 10, 2017. Dedicated Tensor Cores accelerated matrix arithmetic, aligning silicon execution more directly with the multiply-and-accumulate structure of deep learning instead of relying only on general-purpose arithmetic lanes.

title: GPT: generative pretraining for language understanding
significance: A decoder-only Transformer pretrained on unlabeled text transferred to supervised language tasks, helping establish the GPT approach.

source.title: Radford et al. — Improving Language Understanding by Generative Pre-Training

title: GPT-2: broader zero-shot transfer
significance: A larger language model demonstrated that a next-token objective could support multiple tasks through suitable text context, without separate task-specific training in the reported zero-shot setting.

source.title: Radford et al. — Language Models are Unsupervised Multitask Learners

title: GPT-3 and empirical scaling laws
significance: Large autoregressive models showed broad few-shot capabilities while scaling studies quantified relationships among resources and loss.

source.title: Brown et al. — Language Models are Few-Shot Learners

title: GLU variants improve Transformer feed-forward blocks
significance: Shazeer evaluated gated alternatives including SwiGLU and GEGLU in Transformer feed-forward sublayers, finding improvements over the tested ReLU and GELU baselines.

title: Large-model tensor, pipeline, and data parallelism analyzed together
significance: The Megatron-LM study quantified interactions between parallelism strategies, emphasizing that model partitioning and hardware communication must be designed together.

source.title: Narayanan et al. — Efficient Large-Scale Language Model Training

title: RoFormer proposes rotary position embedding
significance: The RoFormer preprint introduced RoPE, encoding position through query/key rotations so their interaction includes relative displacement.

title: Switch Transformer simplifies sparse routing
significance: The Switch Transformer preprint investigated top-one expert routing and training techniques that made very large sparse Transformer models easier to train; it was published in JMLR in 2022.

title: Deduplication is measured as a training intervention
significance: Lee and colleagues showed that removing repeated training material could reduce memorized output and train–test overlap while preserving or improving measured accuracy. Their preprint preceded ACL 2022 publication.

source.title: Lee et al. — Deduplicating Training Data Makes Language Models Better

title: Compute-optimal training
significance: The Chinchilla study emphasized balancing model size with sufficient training data under a fixed compute budget.

title: FlashAttention
significance: IO-aware attention showed how a better algorithm can reduce memory traffic while retaining exact attention semantics.

title: Hopper adds FP8 Transformer Engine and asynchronous tensor movement
significance: Introduced on March 22, 2022, Hopper combined a Transformer Engine with FP8 support, Tensor Memory Accelerator transfers, and thread-block clusters. The architecture extended both numerical efficiency and explicit coordination of movement and computation across the GPU hierarchy.

title: Grace CPU Superchip announces server LPDDR5X integration
significance: The March 2022 Grace CPU Superchip announcement described an LPDDR5X memory subsystem with error correction in a data-center CPU platform. This is a Grace platform milestone, not the invention of LPDDR memory.

title: InstructGPT combines demonstrations and preferences
significance: Ouyang and colleagues reported supervised instruction tuning followed by preference-based reinforcement learning, showing that user preference could improve without merely increasing parameter count.

source.title: Ouyang et al. — Training Language Models to Follow Instructions with Human Feedback

title: ReAct interleaves language-model reasoning and actions
significance: Yao and colleagues explored alternating reasoning and actions that gather observations from external environments. The preprint appeared in 2022 and the conference version at ICLR 2023.

source.title: Yao et al. — ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models

title: PagedAttention
significance: Block-based KV management connected serving efficiency to careful handling of growing and shrinking request memory.

title: Levels of AGI separates breadth from performance
significance: Morris and colleagues proposed a framework for comparing capability breadth and performance while treating deployment autonomy separately, making progress claims more explicit than a single benchmark score.

source.title: Morris et al. — Levels of AGI for Operationalizing Progress on the Path to AGI

title: Blackwell extends acceleration from multiple dies to rack-scale systems
significance: Announced on March 18, 2024, Blackwell joined two large logic dies within one GPU and paired new numerical formats with stronger GPU interconnect. Grace Blackwell systems brought CPU, GPU memory, scale-up networking, power, and cooling into a more tightly coordinated architecture; no specific proprietary model’s deployment is implied.

title: GB200 NVL72 rack-scale architecture announced
significance: The documented example integrates 72 GPUs through a large NVLink domain with purpose-built communication and liquid-cooling infrastructure. It illustrates system-level co-design rather than proving a model capability by itself.

title: CUTLASS 3.8 exposes Blackwell Tensor Memory
significance: The February 2025 CUTLASS 3.8 release added Blackwell SM100 support and exposed Tensor Memory as a distinct storage location, along with operations that move values between registers, shared memory, and Tensor Memory.

title: GPT-6 Astra released through the OpenAI API
significance: The September 3 API changelog announced Astra for complex tasks using supplied context and tools, with tool calling through the Responses API. This is a product milestone, not a declaration of AGI.
